B. Act, because the money will be received through a regulated bank in any event

C. Act, provided the additional fee is held in client account until identity is provided

D. Decline to act, because identity must be verified before the relationship begins

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Decline to act, because identity must be verified before the relationship begins): verification of identity from a reliable independent source is required before the business relationship is established, so a firm cannot proceed where the client refuses to provide it, and the refusal combined with urgency and an inflated fee is itself a serious red flag. Option A is wrong because recording a refusal documents the breach rather than curing it. Receipt of money through a regulated bank does not discharge the firm's own due diligence obligation.

223. A fee earner is uneasy about the funding of a purchase but tells his supervisor that he will first ask the client some searching questions, look at the client's business online, and only report if his own enquiries confirm the concern. Is that approach correct?

A. No, because he must not decide the suspicion is unfounded or investigate the client

B. Yes, because a report should not be made until the suspicion has been verified

C. Yes, because the firm's reporting officer expects a fully evidenced internal report

D. No, because he must report the matter directly to the National Crime Agency

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (No, because he must not decide the suspicion is unfounded or investigate the client): a fee earner does not decide for himself that a suspicion is unfounded and does not investigate the client, because that risks alerting the client and delays a report that should be made once suspicion exists. Option B is wrong because the threshold is suspicion, not proof, so waiting for verification postpones the duty. The report goes to the reporting officer first, who decides whether to report to the National Crime Agency.

224. Acting for a buyer, a solicitor discovers that the seller's adult son lives at the property, contributed a substantial sum to the original purchase price and is not a registered proprietor. Nothing about him appears anywhere on the register. What is the risk and the correct step before exchange?

A. No risk arises, because only registered entries bind a purchaser for value

B. He must be registered as a joint proprietor before contracts are exchanged

C. He must be granted a tenancy so that his position is properly disclosed

D. His occupation may override, so obtain a signed release before exchange

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (His occupation may override, so obtain a signed release before exchange): the interest of a person in actual occupation is the overriding interest that matters most in practice, and a contributor in occupation may have an equitable interest binding the buyer despite the register. The safe course is a signed release from him, or having him join in the transfer. Option A is wrong precisely because an overriding interest binds without appearing on the register, which is what makes the enquiry about occupiers essential.

225. A firm's money laundering reporting officer has received an internal report about the funding of a purchase, and agrees that there are reasonable grounds for suspicion. Completion is scheduled for next week. What is the reporting officer's function at this point?

A. To interview the client and to obtain a full written explanation of the funding

B. To advise the fee earner whether the retainer may lawfully be terminated now

C. To decide whether to report to the National Crime Agency and seek a defence

D. To notify the seller's solicitor so that the completion date can be moved back

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (To decide whether to report to the National Crime Agency and seek a defence): the reporting officer decides whether the matter should be reported externally to the National Crime Agency and, where consent is needed to proceed, seeks a defence against money laundering. Option A is wrong because questioning the client is a form of investigating the client and risks tipping off. Telling the seller's solicitor why completion cannot proceed would itself risk making a prejudicial disclosure.

226. A seller is selling a paddock behind his own house and proposes that the buyer should be allowed to cross the seller's drive to reach the road. The buyer's solicitor wants the right to be a legal easement binding future owners of the drive. What is required?

A. A written note of the agreement signed by the seller before completion takes place

B. An express grant by deed for a term equivalent to a fee simple absolute

C. A statutory declaration by the seller confirming the buyer's long user of the drive

D. An entry in the property register of the paddock recording the informal permission

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (An express grant by deed for a term equivalent to a fee simple absolute): a legal easement must be granted by deed and held for an interest equivalent to a fee simple absolute in possession or a term of years absolute, and on a sale of part that grant is made in the transfer deed itself and must then be completed by registration, because the express grant of an easement is a registrable disposition which does not operate at law until it is registered. Option D is wrong because a register entry recording nothing more than an informal permission creates no easement at all; the deed of grant, completed by registration, is what produces the legal right. A signed note or a declaration of user does not amount to an express legal grant.

227. Two solicitors exchange contracts by telephone using a Law Society formula. Each undertakes to hold his client's signed part to the other's order and to post it the same day. The seller's solicitor then forgets to post his client's part for a week. What is the position of the solicitor who gave that undertaking?

A. The undertaking binds the firm only if it was later confirmed in writing

B. The undertaking is personally binding on the solicitor who gave it

C. The undertaking lapses once the contract has become binding on exchange

D. The undertaking binds the client, who must indemnify the other party

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The undertaking is personally binding on the solicitor who gave it): exchange by telephone under a Law Society formula proceeds on undertakings to hold the signed part to the other's order and to post it the same day, and such an undertaking is personally binding on the solicitor who gives it. Option A is wrong because an undertaking given orally on the telephone is binding without any written confirmation, which is exactly why the formulae are used with care. The client is not the party who gave the undertaking.

228. A firm is instructed by a new client resident in a country identified as presenting a high risk of money laundering. The client wishes to buy a London flat and is providing the whole price himself. The fee earner proposes to carry out the firm's usual identity checks and nothing more. Is that sufficient?

A. Yes, provided the identity documents are certified by a lawyer in that country

B. Yes, because the firm's standard procedures already meet the regulatory requirement

C. No, because a high risk third country connection calls for enhanced due diligence

D. No, because the firm must decline to act for any client resident outside the country

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (No, because a high risk third country connection calls for enhanced due diligence): enhanced due diligence applies where the risk is higher, and a connection to a high risk third country is one of the standard triggers, alongside a politically exposed person. Option A is wrong because certification goes to the reliability of the documents and does not raise the level of due diligence being applied. Option D overstates the position, since foreign residence does not by itself prevent a firm from acting.

229. A buyer's solicitor is advising on a detached house in a village outside Norwich, where several neighbouring houses are on private treatment plants. She needs to confirm that the property is connected to mains water and a public sewer, and whether any public sewer runs within the garden. Which enquiry answers that?

A. The local authority search made of the district council for the area

B. The environmental search covering contaminated land, flooding and ground stability

C. Pre contract enquiries raised of the seller about the services generally

D. The drainage and water enquiries addressed to the water and sewerage undertaker

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (The drainage and water enquiries addressed to the water and sewerage undertaker): drainage and water enquiries confirm whether the property is connected to mains water and to a public sewer, and whether a public sewer runs within the boundary, which matters because building over a sewer is restricted. Option C is wrong because the seller's own answers are not an independent confirmation from the undertaker and a seller may simply not know. The local search and environmental search each answer different questions.

230. A landlord wants to recover a shop at the end of a protected business tenancy so that he can demolish and rebuild the parade. His solicitor is drafting the section 25 notice and is considering what the notice itself has to say. What must the notice state?

A. The rent the landlord would accept if the tenant were granted a renewal

B. Whether renewal is opposed, and if so on which statutory ground

C. The identity of any incoming tenant to whom the premises will be let

D. The date on which the landlord's building contractor will take possession

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (Whether renewal is opposed, and if so on which statutory ground): a section 25 notice must state whether the landlord opposes the grant of a new tenancy and, if it does, the statutory ground of opposition relied on, here the intention to demolish and reconstruct. Option A is wrong because proposals for the terms of a new tenancy are only required where the landlord is not opposing renewal, and the notice here is an opposed one. The landlord's contractual and letting arrangements are not part of the notice.

231. A buyer's solicitor sees that the proprietorship register of a registered leasehold flat gives the class of title as good leasehold. The buyer is borrowing from a high street lender whose instructions require absolute title. The buyer asks what good leasehold means in practice. What is the correct advice?

A. The freehold title was not proved, so insurance or lender consent is needed

B. The lease has under eighty years unexpired, so an extension is needed

C. The registered proprietor is a personal representative, so a second trustee is needed

D. The boundaries are unproved, so a determined boundary application is needed

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The freehold title was not proved, so insurance or lender consent is needed): good leasehold title means the registrar was satisfied as to the lease itself but the superior freehold title was not deduced, so the grant of the lease is not guaranteed. Because a lender ordinarily expects absolute title, the practical answer is title indemnity insurance or the lender's express consent. Option B is wrong because the unexpired term is a separate valuation and lending question and has nothing to do with the class of title entered on the register.

232. A client is completing two purchases on the same day, a house in Chester and a holiday cottage near Aberystwyth. She asks her solicitor which tax applies to each purchase. No rates, bands or thresholds are in issue at this stage of the advice. What is the correct advice?

A. Stamp duty land tax applies to both, because they complete on one day

B. Land transaction tax applies to both, because one buyer is purchasing both

C. Stamp duty land tax applies in Wales and land transaction tax in England

D. Stamp duty land tax applies in England and land transaction tax in Wales

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Stamp duty land tax applies in England and land transaction tax in Wales): a land transaction in England attracts stamp duty land tax while a land transaction in Wales attracts land transaction tax, and the two are genuinely different taxes with different legislation and reliefs. Option C is wrong because it reverses the position, which is a common slip. The identity of the buyer and the fact that both purchases complete on the same day do not change which territory's tax applies to which property.

233. On a purchase of unregistered land, the buyer's solicitor must discover whether any restrictive covenant or estate contract binds the land. The epitome names four different estate owners over the period since the root of title. Against what does the solicitor search at the Land Charges Department?

A. The address of the property and its postcode within the relevant district

B. The names of the estate owners, for their respective periods of ownership

C. The title number allocated to the land on any earlier first registration

D. The parcels clause of the earliest conveyance contained in the epitome

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The names of the estate owners, for their respective periods of ownership): the Land Charges Department register is a names based register, so the search is made against the names of the estate owners and for the periods during which each of them owned. Option A is wrong because a search by address or description is the local land charges search made of the local authority, which answers an entirely different question. Unregistered land has no title number, and the parcels clause describes extent rather than encumbrances.

234. Two days before completion of a purchase, a firm receives the balance of the price from a company account in a name the client has never mentioned. The client, when asked, says only that a business associate is helping out and asks the firm to press on. What is the correct characterisation?

A. A routine funding arrangement, since the money has arrived in cleared funds

B. A red flag, being an unexplained third party paying part of the price

C. A conflict of interest, because the firm now acts for two separate clients

D. A breach of undertaking, because the money came from an unexpected source

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (A red flag, being an unexplained third party paying part of the price): an unexplained third party paying all or part of the price is one of the classic money laundering red flags, and a vague explanation offered under time pressure does not answer it. Option A is wrong because the money being cleared says nothing about its origin, and cleared funds from an unexplained source are exactly what a launderer wants. Receiving unexpected money does not by itself create a conflict of interest or breach an undertaking.

235. A client instructs a firm on the purchase of a shop with a flat above. He does not read the report on title, is unconcerned that the lease of the flat has only nine years left, and tells the solicitor to agree whatever contract terms the seller wants. What is the significance of that behaviour?

A. It shows the client trusts the firm, which reduces the risk of a complaint

B. It is a red flag, because a client indifferent to the property and terms is suspicious

C. It is irrelevant, because the client is entitled to give whatever instructions he wishes

D. It requires the firm to obtain the client's written confirmation of each instruction

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (It is a red flag, because a client indifferent to the property and terms is suspicious): indifference to the property or to the contract terms is a recognised red flag, because a buyer whose real objective is to move money does not care what is being bought or on what terms. Option C is wrong because a client's freedom to instruct does not displace the firm's separate regulatory duty to assess risk. Written confirmations are good file practice but do not address the underlying concern.

236. A client is funding her purchase from three sources: her savings, a gift from her mother, and the proceeds of the sale of her existing house. Her solicitor is deciding what evidence to obtain for each element before exchange. Which set of documents is appropriate?

A. Bank statements showing accumulation, a gift letter, and the sale completion statement

B. A signed declaration from the client listing each of the three funding sources

C. The mother's passport, the client's payslips, and the buyer's mortgage offer

D. An estate agent's valuation of the existing house and a savings account number

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Bank statements showing accumulation, a gift letter, and the sale completion statement): source of funds is answered with evidence appropriate to each element, so savings are shown by statements demonstrating accumulation, a gift by a letter from the donor, and sale proceeds by the completion statement from the related sale. Option B is wrong because the client's own declaration is an assertion rather than evidence, and the whole point of the exercise is independent corroboration. A valuation and an account number evidence neither origin nor accumulation.

237. A buyer's solicitor is advising on interests that could bind the buyer even though nothing about them appears on the register. The seller says she lives alone, but a lodger has been in the property for two years paying rent weekly. Which statement about overriding interests is correct?

A. An interest of a person in actual occupation may bind the buyer

B. Overriding interests were abolished when electronic conveyancing was introduced

C. Only interests noted in the charges register can bind a later buyer

D. A buyer is bound only by interests the seller discloses in enquiries

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (An interest of a person in actual occupation may bind the buyer): overriding interests bind a buyer without appearing on the register, and the one that matters most in practice is the interest of a person in actual occupation, which is why occupation is asked about at interview and again in enquiries. Option C is wrong because it states the opposite of the overriding interest principle and would make enquiries about occupiers pointless. A seller's failure to disclose does not protect a buyer against an interest that overrides.

238. A tenant of a shop wants to assign her lease to a well funded national retailer. The lease contains a covenant by the tenant not to assign the whole or any part of the premises. There is no reference anywhere in the lease to the landlord's consent. What is the tenant's position?

A. She may assign, because the landlord cannot unreasonably withhold its consent

B. The covenant is absolute, so assignment is prohibited without a variation

C. She may assign, because the proposed assignee is plainly financially strong

D. The covenant is qualified, so the landlord must respond within a reasonable time

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The covenant is absolute, so assignment is prohibited without a variation): an absolute covenant against assignment prohibits assignment outright, and the tenant can only proceed if the landlord agrees to waive the covenant or to vary the lease, which the landlord is free to refuse. Option D is wrong because the statutory protections about unreasonable refusal and a reasonable response time attach to a qualified covenant, that is one requiring consent, not to an absolute prohibition. The assignee's financial strength is irrelevant where no consent mechanism exists.

239. A buyer is purchasing a flat in a block of thirty. The management company has just consulted the tenants about replacing the roof and the lifts. The reserve fund holds very little and the seller is in arrears. The buyer asks whether any of this affects her. What is the correct advice?

A. The consultation binds only the current tenant, so the buyer is unaffected

B. The buyer takes the flat free of any service charge arising before completion

C. Arrears and forthcoming major works are a real financial risk to investigate

D. The landlord must fund major works itself where the reserve fund is inadequate

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (Arrears and forthcoming major works are a real financial risk to investigate): the service charge apportionment, the reserve fund and any planned major works must be investigated, because arrears and a forthcoming major works bill are a genuine financial exposure for the buyer. Option B is wrong because whether pre completion arrears can be pursued depends on the lease and on what is agreed and retained on completion, so a buyer should never simply assume immunity. A landlord recovers major works costs through the service charge rather than funding them itself.

240. A company buys a freehold factory in Rotherham with the assistance of a bank loan secured by a legal charge over the factory. The company's solicitor is listing every post completion registration the transaction requires, in addition to the Land Registry application. Which further registration is needed, and within what period?

A. Registration at the local land charges registry within two months of completion

B. Registration with the Welsh Revenue Authority within thirty days of completion

C. Registration of the charge at Companies House within twenty one days of creation

D. Registration of the charge at the Land Charges Department within fifteen days

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (Registration of the charge at Companies House within twenty one days of creation): a charge created by a company must be registered at Companies House within twenty one days of its creation, in addition to registration of the charge against the title at HM Land Registry. Option B is wrong because the property is in England, so the Welsh Revenue Authority has no role, and a tax return is not a registration of the charge in any event. The Land Charges Department concerns unregistered land and does not register company charges.

241. A client instructing a firm on a substantial purchase in Oxford has produced a bank statement showing the full purchase price sitting in her current account. Her solicitor now wants to understand her source of wealth as well. Which question is the solicitor actually asking?

A. Which account the completion money will be sent from on the day

B. Whether the client has any borrowing secured against her other assets

C. How the client came by her wealth overall, whether by employment or inheritance

D. Whether the price agreed is a fair reflection of the property's market value

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (How the client came by her wealth overall, whether by employment or inheritance): source of wealth asks how the client came by her wealth generally, for example employment, a business sale, inheritance or investment, and it is a separate question from where the money for this purchase is coming from. Option A is wrong because the transferring account goes to the mechanics of payment and answers neither question. The price against value is a red flag consideration rather than a description of source of wealth.

242. A solicitor is instructed by the seller of a registered freehold house in Exeter, and the transaction is proceeding under the residential protocol. She is assembling the pre contract package to send to the buyer's solicitor. Which set of items should that package contain?

A. Official copies, the local search result and the buyer's mortgage offer

B. The transfer deed, a completion statement and the mortgage redemption figure

C. Official copies and title plan, the draft contract and the protocol forms

D. The energy certificate, the survey report and the buyer's identity documents

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (Official copies and title plan, the draft contract and the protocol forms): the seller's solicitor prepares official copies of the register and title plan, the draft contract and the protocol forms, typically the property information form and the fittings and contents form. Option A is wrong because the local search is commissioned by the buyer's solicitor and the buyer's mortgage offer is nothing to do with the seller. The transfer deed, completion statement and redemption figure all belong to the completion and post completion stages.

243. A neighbour claims an equitable easement to park two cars on a corner of the registered land being sold, arising out of an informal written arrangement made in 2019. He does not occupy the land and parks there only occasionally. Nothing appears on the register. How should the neighbour have protected the right?

A. By registering a land charge at the Land Charges Department against the owner

B. By applying to be registered as a joint proprietor of the corner of land

C. By occupying the corner of land continuously so as to override on a sale

D. By entering a notice in the charges register to protect the right's priority

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (By entering a notice in the charges register to protect the right's priority): in registered land the priority of a third party interest such as an option or an equitable easement is protected by a notice in the charges register. Option A is wrong because the Land Charges Department register applies to unregistered land, and the title here is registered. Becoming a joint proprietor would give ownership rather than an easement, and occasional parking is unlikely to amount to actual occupation capable of overriding.

244. The proprietorship register of a registered title contains a restriction stating that no disposition is to be registered without a certificate signed by the management company. Completion is fixed for ten days' time and the certificate has not been requested. What should the buyer's solicitor do about the restriction?

A. Ignore it, because a restriction does not affect the validity of a transfer

B. Apply to cancel the restriction immediately after completion has taken place

C. Report it to the lender only, since it concerns the charge alone

D. Obtain the certificate before completion, or the application will be rejected

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Obtain the certificate before completion, or the application will be rejected): a restriction controls whether a disposition can be registered, so where it requires a third party's consent or certificate that document must be obtained before completion or the registration application will be rejected. Option A is wrong because although the transfer may be valid between the parties, the buyer will be left unable to perfect the legal title, which is the whole point of the purchase. Cancelling a restriction after completion is not available where the restriction is properly entered and still applies.

245. A solicitor acts for the buyer of a warehouse in Hull. The agreed price is roughly three times what comparable units in the same estate have sold for, and the buyer has not questioned it. The buyer is content to complete quickly and asks no questions about condition. What should concern the solicitor?

A. A price obviously out of line with value is a recognised laundering red flag

B. The buyer may have overpaid and could have a claim against the selling agent

C. The lender's valuation will resolve the point, so the solicitor need not act

D. An overvalue creates a higher tax liability which the buyer should be warned about

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (A price obviously out of line with value is a recognised laundering red flag): a price obviously out of line with value in either direction is a recognised red flag, because an inflated or deflated price is a way of moving value, and a buyer indifferent to that mismatch compounds the concern. Option C is wrong because there is no lender here and, in any event, a solicitor's own obligation does not pass to a valuer. A possible claim against the agent and the tax consequence are real but secondary points.

246. Amara has agreed to buy a freehold house in Shrewsbury. Her solicitor has received the official copies, the draft contract and the protocol forms from the seller's solicitor. Amara asks at what point in the transaction the deposit becomes payable and the completion date becomes fixed. What is the correct advice?

A. On completion, when the purchase money and the transfer deed are exchanged

B. When the mortgage offer is formally issued by Amara's chosen lender

C. On exchange of contracts, once title, searches and finance are satisfactory

D. When the local authority search result is returned to her solicitor

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (On exchange of contracts, once title, searches and finance are satisfactory): exchange is the moment the parties become contractually bound, the completion date is fixed and the deposit is paid, and it should not happen until title, searches, enquiries, finance and the contract terms are all satisfactory. Option A is wrong because by completion the deposit has long been held and the date has already been fixed. A mortgage offer and a search result are both preconditions to exchange rather than the trigger for the deposit.

247. A client's completion money has been received by the firm. The client then telephones to say that he has decided not to buy after all, and asks that the money be sent to an account in a different name in another country. He offers no reason for the change. What should the solicitor do?

A. Return the money to the account it came from and close the file promptly

B. Send the money as instructed, since the client owns it and has changed his mind

C. Ask the client to confirm the instruction in writing and then send the money

D. Treat this as a classic laundering method and report a suspicion internally

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Treat this as a classic laundering method and report a suspicion internally): a transaction aborted after the money has arrived, with a request for repayment to a different account or a third party, is a classic method of using a client account to clean money, and it should be treated as such by making an internal report. Option A is wrong because although returning funds to source is safer than sending them onward, it still disposes of possibly criminal property without the report being made. A written confirmation adds nothing.

248. A seller is registered with possessory title to a strip of garden which was acquired many years ago by long use. The buyer's lender has queried the entry and asked what protection the buyer will have. The buyer's solicitor explains what possessory title means. Which explanation is correct?

A. Ownership is guaranteed, but the land cannot be charged for twelve years

B. Ownership is provisional and lapses automatically after twelve years of use

C. The title depends on a lease whose superior title was not produced

D. Rights subsisting when the title was registered are not excluded by registration

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Rights subsisting when the title was registered are not excluded by registration): possessory title is granted where the proprietor is in possession but full documentary title was not deduced, so registration does not affect adverse rights subsisting at the date of first registration. Option C is wrong because that describes good leasehold title, where the lease is accepted but the superior freehold was not proved. Possessory title does not lapse automatically and does not prevent the land from being charged.

249. A firm is instructed on the purchase of a large country house by a client who holds senior public office in a foreign state. The purchase price is substantial and the funds are coming from an overseas account. What level of due diligence does the firm have to apply, and why?

A. Enhanced due diligence, because a politically exposed person presents higher risk

B. Standard due diligence, because the client holds a legitimate public office

C. Simplified due diligence, because a public official's income is a matter of record

D. No further due diligence, because the funds are coming through a regulated bank

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Enhanced due diligence, because a politically exposed person presents higher risk): enhanced due diligence applies where the risk is higher, and a politically exposed person is the standard example, as is a connection to a high risk third country. Option B is wrong because holding public office is precisely what triggers the higher risk category rather than reassuring the firm. Money arriving through a regulated bank does not remove the firm's own obligation, because the firm is separately within the regulated sector and owes its own duties.

250. A buyer is purchasing a new house in Stoke on Trent built on a former industrial site, close to a river which has burst its banks in the past. His solicitor wants to assess whether the land may be contaminated and whether the property carries a real risk of flooding. Which step addresses those risks?

A. An environmental search, which assesses contaminated land and the flood risk

B. The local authority search, which lists planning and enforcement matters recorded

C. The drainage and water enquiries made of the water and sewerage undertaker

D. A bankruptcy search made against the seller before the contracts are exchanged

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (An environmental search, which assesses contaminated land and the flood risk): the environmental search is the search directed at contaminated land and flood risk, which are exactly the concerns raised by a former industrial site beside a river. Option B is wrong because the local search reports what the council itself records about planning, highways and enforcement, and does not assess contamination or flooding. A bankruptcy search is a pre completion search made for the lender against the borrower, not the seller.

251. A contract for the sale of a house incorporates the Standard Conditions of Sale, and then adds a special condition providing that the deposit is to be held by the seller's solicitor as agent for the seller. The buyer's solicitor spots the inconsistency with the standard condition. What is the effect?

A. The special condition prevails, so the deposit may be released before completion

B. The standard condition prevails, so the deposit must be held as stakeholder

C. Both conditions are void for inconsistency, so no deposit is payable at all

D. The buyer may choose which of the two inconsistent conditions is to apply

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The special condition prevails, so the deposit may be released before completion): a contract incorporates the standard conditions as amended by the special conditions the parties negotiate, so where a special condition contradicts a standard condition the special condition governs. Option B is wrong because it inverts that relationship and would make special conditions pointless. The buyer's solicitor should therefore advise on the loss of stakeholder protection and consider objecting to the clause rather than treating it as void or optional.

252. A buyer's solicitor also acts for the buyer's lender on a standard residential mortgage. Contracts have been exchanged and completion is next week, so the firm must requisition the mortgage advance in good time. Before the advance is released to the firm, what must the solicitor provide to the lender?

A. A copy of the signed contract and the buyer's identity documents

B. The completed transfer deed executed by both the seller and the buyer

C. An undertaking to register the legal charge within twenty one days

D. A certificate of title confirming the title is good and marketable

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (A certificate of title confirming the title is good and marketable): a solicitor acting for both buyer and lender must check the title, comply with the lender's handbook instructions and give a certificate of title before the advance is released. Option B is wrong because the transfer deed is not completed and dated until completion itself, which is after the advance has been drawn down. Identity documents and a contract copy are file matters that do not discharge the certificate of title obligation.

253. A client is buying a flat in Nottingham for cash. Her solicitor asks her to explain her source of funds. The client replies that she has worked in banking for twenty years and earns a substantial salary. The solicitor is not satisfied. What is the correct explanation of what source of funds means?

A. Where the money for this particular purchase comes from, evidenced by documents

B. How the client accumulated her overall wealth across her working lifetime

C. Whether the client's income is sufficient to service any borrowing taken

D. Which bank the money will be transferred from on the day of completion

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Where the money for this particular purchase comes from, evidenced by documents): source of funds asks where the money for this purchase comes from and is answered with evidence, such as bank statements showing accumulation, a mortgage offer, a gift letter or a completion statement from a related sale. Option B is wrong because that describes source of wealth, which is a different question about how the client came by her wealth overall. Naming the transferring bank identifies a route rather than an origin.

254. A new client wants to buy a house in Blackpool for cash with no mortgage, wants to complete within five days, has not visited the property and does not want a survey. He has offered the full asking price without negotiation. What should the solicitor conclude from this combination of features?

A. Nothing, because a cash buyer is entitled to complete as quickly as possible

B. That the client is a first time investor who requires additional practical guidance

C. That these are recognised red flags requiring scrutiny before the matter proceeds

D. That the firm should simply obtain a written waiver of the survey advice given

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (That these are recognised red flags requiring scrutiny before the matter proceeds): a rushed cash purchase with no lender carrying out its own checks, and a client indifferent to the property itself, are recognised red flags, and several appearing together call for real scrutiny rather than speed. Option A is wrong because it treats each feature in isolation and ignores the pattern, which is what makes this combination significant. A waiver of survey advice protects the file on negligence but does nothing about the laundering risk.

255. Completion of a registered purchase took place on 3 June 2027, following an official search of the whole title with priority made a few days earlier. The buyer's solicitor is dealing with the tax return and then the registration application. Why does the timing of the registration application matter so much?

A. It must be made within the search priority period or priority is lost

B. It must be made within twenty one days or the buyer's charge is void

C. It must be made before the seller's existing mortgage is formally redeemed

D. It must be made before the tax return is submitted to the revenue authority

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (It must be made within the search priority period or priority is lost): the official search of the whole title confers a priority period, and the application to register the transfer and any new charge must be made within it, or priority against intervening entries is lost. Option B is wrong because twenty one days is the Companies House deadline for a charge created by a company, which is a different registration with a different consequence. Redemption of the seller's mortgage and the tax return are separate steps in the post completion sequence.

256. Four business partners bought an office as beneficial joint tenants. They contributed the price in the proportions forty, thirty, twenty and ten per cent. One partner now serves a valid written notice of severance on the other three. He asks what share he now holds in equity. What is the correct advice?

A. He holds forty per cent, because severance restores the original contributions made

B. He holds a one quarter share, because severance produces equal shares between them

C. He holds no share until a declaration of trust is signed by all four

D. He holds a share to be determined by the court on an application by him

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (He holds a one quarter share, because severance produces equal shares between them): severance of an equitable joint tenancy gives the severing co owner an equal aliquot share, so where there are four of them he takes one quarter as a tenant in common regardless of what he originally contributed, and the other three continue to hold the remaining three quarters as joint tenants between themselves. Option A is wrong because a joint tenancy means the co owners own the whole together and the original contributions were absorbed into that, which is why a declaration of trust recording intended shares matters so much at the outset. No court application is needed for severance to take effect.

257. A transfer form has been signed by the seller alone at his kitchen table with nobody else present. The witness name and address on the signature page were written in afterwards by his wife, who was upstairs at the time he signed. The buyer's solicitor considers the execution. What is the position?

A. The deed is valid, because the witness details appear on the signature page

B. The deed is not validly executed, because the witness must attest the signature

C. The deed is valid, because a spouse is a permitted witness to a transfer

D. The deed is not valid, because a transfer must be signed by both parties

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The deed is not validly executed, because the witness must attest the signature): a deed must be clear on its face that it is a deed, be signed in the presence of a witness who attests the signature, and be delivered, so a witness who was not present when the signature was made cannot attest it. Option C is wrong because although a spouse is not automatically disqualified, presence at signing is the requirement that fails here. A transfer of the whole for value does not always require the buyer's signature.

258. After exchange but before completion a storm removes part of the roof of the house being bought. Neither party is at fault and the property remains usable as a dwelling. The buyer asks who bears the loss. The Standard Conditions of Sale apply without amendment. What is the correct advice?

A. The seller bears the risk and must transfer the property in its exchanged state

B. The loss falls on the buyer, who must complete and claim on her insurance

C. The price is reduced by the cost of the repair as a matter of law

D. The buyer may rescind because the property is no longer as she contracted for

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The seller bears the risk and must transfer the property in its exchanged state): under the Standard Conditions of Sale the seller retains the risk until completion, so accidental damage before completion is the seller's problem and the buyer may require the property in the physical state it was in at exchange, fair wear and tear excepted. Option B states the position under the Standard Commercial Property Conditions, where risk does pass on exchange, and is the commonest confusion on this topic. Option D would be open to the buyer only if the damage had made the property unusable for its purpose, which these facts exclude, and option C invents a price adjustment the conditions do not provide.

259. A tenant occupies a workshop under a lease which was properly contracted out of the security of tenure provisions before it was granted, using the statutory notice and declaration. The term expires on 31 March 2027. The tenant asks whether she can require a new lease at that date. What is the correct advice?

A. She may require a new tenancy, because she has occupied for business purposes

B. She may require a new tenancy if the landlord has no ground of opposition

C. She may remain until the landlord serves a section 25 notice ending the tenancy

D. She has no right of renewal and must leave when the contractual term expires

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (She has no right of renewal and must leave when the contractual term expires): where the parties validly contracted out using the statutory notice and declaration procedure before the grant, the tenancy has no security of tenure, so it ends on the contractual expiry date with no right of renewal. Option C is wrong because a section 25 notice is the mechanism for ending a protected tenancy, and a contracted out tenancy simply expires without one. Business occupation alone does not confer protection once the tenancy has been contracted out.

260. A buyer tells her solicitor that she does not want to pay for a survey, because her lender is instructing a valuer and she assumes that report will tell her whether the house is sound. The property is a Victorian terrace with visible cracking to the rear wall. What is the correct advice?

A. The valuation is a survey, so a further inspection would only duplicate cost

B. The seller warrants the condition of the property under the standard conditions

C. The lender's valuation is not a survey and remains the buyer's responsibility

D. The local authority search will disclose any structural defects in the building

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (The lender's valuation is not a survey and remains the buyer's responsibility): the lender's valuation is carried out for the lender's own lending purposes and is not a survey, and commissioning a survey is the buyer's own responsibility, which matters particularly on an older property showing cracking. Option B is wrong because caveat emptor governs condition and the standard conditions contain no warranty that the property is sound. The local search reports council records and says nothing about structural condition.

261. A seller is transferring the whole of a registered freehold title in Durham to a single buyer. The land is not being divided, no new easements or covenants are being created, and the price is paid in full on completion. The buyer's solicitor is preparing the transfer deed. Which form should she use?

A. Form TR1, which transfers the whole of a registered title

B. Form TP1, which transfers part of a registered title only

C. Form AP1, which applies to change the register after completion

D. Form OS1, which searches the whole title with priority before completion

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Form TR1, which transfers the whole of a registered title): the transfer deed for the whole of a registered title is Land Registry form TR1, and a TP1 is used only where part of a title is being sold off. Option B is wrong because nothing is being divided here, so a transfer of part with its plan and new covenants is unnecessary. Form AP1 is the application to change the register and form OS1 is the pre completion priority search, neither of which is a transfer deed.

262. A landlord is granting a five year lease of a shop in Taunton and does not want the tenant to acquire a right to renew at the end of the term. The tenant is willing to accept that. The lease has not yet been granted. What must be done, and when?

A. Nothing, because a lease under seven years never carries security of tenure

B. A term must be inserted excluding renewal, effective once the lease is registered

C. The statutory notice and declaration procedure must be completed before the grant

D. The landlord must serve a section 25 notice on the tenant before the grant

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (The statutory notice and declaration procedure must be completed before the grant): a business tenancy has security of tenure under Part II of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954 unless the parties contract out using the statutory notice and declaration procedure, which must be completed before the lease is granted. Option B is wrong because a bare exclusion clause without the statutory procedure does not remove security of tenure, and registration has nothing to do with it. A section 25 notice is used to end or renew a protected tenancy, not to exclude one.

263. A lease of an office suite provides that the tenant shall not assign without the landlord's written consent. The tenant applies for consent to a solvent assignee and hears nothing for four months. The landlord then refuses, giving no reason at all. What is the correct analysis of the landlord's conduct?

A. Consent must not be unreasonably withheld and a response is due reasonably quickly

B. The landlord may refuse for any reason, because the lease requires its consent

C. The tenant may assign without consent once three months have passed since applying

D. The covenant is absolute, so the delay and the refusal are both beyond challenge

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Consent must not be unreasonably withheld and a response is due reasonably quickly): this is a qualified covenant, and statute implies that consent is not to be unreasonably withheld and imposes a duty on the landlord to respond within a reasonable time and to give reasons. Option B is wrong because that is the position under an absolute covenant, and the requirement of consent is precisely what brings the statutory protection into play. There is no rule permitting a tenant simply to assign after a fixed period of silence.

264. Bevan telephones a firm in Cardiff to instruct it on the purchase of a house. He gives his name, the address of the property and the price, and asks the firm to begin work immediately. He has never attended the office. What must the solicitor do before establishing the business relationship?

A. Verify Bevan's identity from a reliable and independent source

B. Obtain a written valuation of the property from a local surveyor

C. Send an approved draft contract to the seller's solicitor for signature

D. Commission the local authority search and the drainage and water enquiries

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Verify Bevan's identity from a reliable and independent source): customer due diligence requires the solicitor to identify the client and verify that identity from a reliable, independent source before the business relationship is established. Option D is wrong because searches are part of investigating the property and can only sensibly follow once the retainer is properly opened. A valuation and a draft contract are steps in the transaction itself, not preconditions to acting.

265. A buyer is purchasing a house in Bridgend. Her solicitor is explaining who deals with the return and the payment of the tax on this transaction, and why the point must be attended to promptly after completion. No rates or thresholds arise. Which statement is correct?

A. HM Revenue and Customs administers the tax on a Welsh land transaction

B. The Welsh Revenue Authority administers the tax on a Welsh land transaction

C. The local authority for the area administers the tax on Welsh transactions

D. HM Land Registry administers the tax as part of the registration process

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The Welsh Revenue Authority administers the tax on a Welsh land transaction): land transaction tax applies to a land transaction in Wales and is administered by the Welsh Revenue Authority, whereas stamp duty land tax in England is administered by HM Revenue and Customs. Option A is wrong because it attributes the Welsh tax to the English collecting authority. The Land Registry deals with registration and the local authority with local land charges, and neither administers this tax.

266. A solicitor is taking instructions from a client buying a leasehold flat with a mortgage. The client wants to run a small dog grooming business from the second bedroom and to keep two dogs. Which matters should the solicitor establish first from the lease itself?

A. The unexpired term, the ground rent, the service charge and the user restrictions

B. The identity of the managing agent and the date of the last service charge demand

C. The seller's own purchase price and the date on which the seller acquired it

D. The energy performance rating of the flat and the age of the boiler installed

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The unexpired term, the ground rent, the service charge and the user restrictions): the lease is the contract and must be read, and the solicitor establishes the unexpired term, the ground rent and any review, the service charge, and any restriction on what the client actually wants to do, which here means user and pet covenants. Option B is wrong because the managing agent's identity is administrative detail that does not answer whether the client's intended use is permitted. The seller's purchase history and the boiler are not lease terms.

267. A landlord has peaceably re entered commercial premises after serious rent arrears, relying on the forfeiture clause. The tenant now has funds available and wants the lease back, and the tenant's bank, which holds a charge over the lease, is equally anxious. What may the tenant and the bank do?

A. Nothing, because peaceable re entry ends the lease and every interest in it

B. Apply for relief from forfeiture, which is open to a tenant and a mortgagee

C. Require the landlord to grant a fresh lease on the same terms as before

D. Apply to the Land Registry to reinstate the leasehold title to the register

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (Apply for relief from forfeiture, which is open to a tenant and a mortgagee): both a tenant and a mortgagee of the lease may apply for relief from forfeiture, and relief is commonly granted where the arrears and the landlord's costs are paid. Option A is wrong because it treats forfeiture as final, when the whole point of relief is that the court can restore the lease. There is no right to compel a landlord to grant a new lease, and registration does not itself decide whether the lease survives.

268. A buyer of a cottage in Cumbria asks her solicitor from what date she needs buildings insurance in force. Contracts are to be exchanged on 12 February 2027, with completion fixed for 12 March 2027. The Standard Conditions of Sale are incorporated without amendment. What is the correct advice?

A. From completion, because the seller retains the risk under those conditions

B. From exchange, because risk passes to the buyer when contracts are exchanged

C. From the mortgage offer, because the lender requires cover from that date

D. From registration, because she has no insurable interest until she is registered

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (From completion, because the seller retains the risk under those conditions): under the Standard Conditions of Sale the seller retains the risk until completion, so the buyer is not obliged to insure from exchange, although a lender will usually require cover and many buyers insure anyway. Option B states the old common law rule, and is also what the Standard Commercial Property Conditions provide, which is exactly why the two are so often confused. Option C mistakes a lender's requirement for the contractual allocation of risk, and option D is wrong because a buyer acquires an insurable interest on exchange, not on registration.

269. A lender has taken a legal charge over a registered freehold house and the charge has been registered against the title. The borrower has fallen seriously into arrears and the lender asks its solicitor what the charge actually gives it. Which answer best describes the lender's position?

A. Ownership of the legal estate, which it may sell as registered proprietor

B. A right to occupy the property jointly with the borrower until arrears are cleared

C. An equitable interest only, which must be protected by a notice on the register

D. A power of sale, a power to appoint a receiver and possession rights

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (A power of sale, a power to appoint a receiver and possession rights): a lender takes a legal charge registered against the title, which gives it a power of sale, a power to appoint a receiver and rights to possession, rather than ownership of the land itself. Option A is wrong because a legal charge does not transfer the legal estate to the lender, who is registered as proprietor of the charge and not of the land. A registered legal charge is a legal interest and is not protected merely by a notice.

270. A buyer intends to erect a fence exactly on the line between her new garden and the neighbouring garden. Her solicitor has the title plan, on which the land is edged red. The buyer asks whether the plan settles the precise position of the boundary. What is the correct advice?

A. The plan shows general boundaries only and does not fix the exact line

B. The plan fixes the boundary because it is an official Land Registry document

C. The plan fixes the boundary unless a neighbour objects within twelve years

D. The plan is indicative only until it is stamped by the local authority

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The plan shows general boundaries only and does not fix the exact line): a title plan shows the extent of the registered land, normally edged red, but it shows general boundaries and does not determine the precise boundary line. Option B is wrong because the official status of the plan does not turn a general boundary into a fixed one, and a separate determined boundary application would be required. Neither an objection period nor local authority stamping has any part in how a title plan operates.

271. A firm has made a report about a client's funding and is awaiting a response. The client telephones and asks angrily why nothing is happening. The fee earner is tempted to say that the firm has had to make a report and that its hands are tied. Why must he not say that?

A. Because the duty of confidentiality is owed to the National Crime Agency instead

B. Because disclosing something likely to prejudice an investigation is an offence

C. Because the client would then be entitled to terminate the retainer immediately

D. Because the firm cannot confirm the report until the agency has replied to it

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (Because disclosing something likely to prejudice an investigation is an offence): once a report has been made, or is being made, it is an offence to disclose anything likely to prejudice an investigation, which is why the client must not be told that a report exists. Option D is wrong because the difficulty is not one of timing or confirmation; the prohibition applies whatever the agency has or has not said. The client's right to end the retainer is beside the point.

272. A firm has made a report to the National Crime Agency and is waiting to hear whether a defence against money laundering will be granted. The contractual completion date falls in three days and the client is pressing hard to complete on time. What must the firm do about completion?

A. Complete on the contractual date, because the report has already been made

B. Complete, but hold the purchase money in client account until a response arrives

C. Complete, provided the client gives a written indemnity against any later loss

D. Not complete until the position with the National Crime Agency is resolved

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Not complete until the position with the National Crime Agency is resolved): until the request for a defence against money laundering is resolved the firm must not complete, because completing would be dealing with property the firm suspects to be criminal property. Option A is wrong because making the report is not itself permission to proceed, and the whole purpose of seeking a defence is that the firm needs the outcome before acting. A client indemnity cannot make a criminal act lawful.

273. Completion of a registered freehold purchase is taking place remotely by telephone and bank transfer on 9 July 2027. The buyer's solicitor has sent the completion money and is waiting to hear from the seller's solicitor. Which answer best describes what actually happens at the moment of completion?

A. The transfer is registered at the Land Registry and the legal title passes

B. The money passes and the transfer deed is dated and released

C. The contract is signed by both parties and the deposit becomes payable

D. The seller's existing mortgage is discharged at the Land Registry by the lender

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (The money passes and the transfer deed is dated and released): on completion the purchase money passes and the transfer deed is dated and released to the buyer's solicitor, and only afterwards does the seller's solicitor redeem the existing mortgage and account to the seller. Option A is wrong because registration is a post completion step, and legal title in registered land passes on registration rather than at completion itself. Signature of the contract and payment of the deposit both happened at exchange.

274. Two brothers hold a house as beneficial joint tenants. One has fallen out with the other and wants his half to pass to his daughter on his death. He does not want to sell and does not want negotiations. He asks his solicitor for the simplest immediate step. What should the solicitor advise?

A. Make a will leaving his share to his daughter, which severs the joint tenancy

B. Apply to HM Land Registry to be registered as sole proprietor of a half

C. Sell his interest to his daughter for value, which is the only method available

D. Serve written notice of severance on his brother, creating a tenancy in common

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (Serve written notice of severance on his brother, creating a tenancy in common): an equitable joint tenancy may be severed by written notice given to the other joint tenants, and that is the simplest unilateral step, producing a tenancy in common in equal shares. Option A is wrong because a will operates only on death, and at the moment of death survivorship has already carried the interest to the survivor, so a will alone cannot sever. Selling to the daughter is one recognised method but it is far from the only one.

275. Three friends hold a property as beneficial joint tenants. Without telling the others, one of them mortgages her interest to a lender to raise money for a business. She then dies a year later. The surviving two claim that the whole beneficial interest has passed to them. What is the correct analysis?

A. The mortgage was an act operating on her share, which severed her joint tenancy

B. The mortgage was void, because a joint tenant has no share capable of charge

C. Survivorship applies, because the other joint tenants never consented to the mortgage

D. The mortgage severed the legal joint tenancy, leaving two legal owners only

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The mortgage was an act operating on her share, which severed her joint tenancy): an equitable joint tenancy is severed by an act of a joint tenant operating on his or her own share, and charging that share is the classic example, so her share became a tenancy in common share and passed under her will or intestacy. Option C is wrong because severance by an act on a share does not require the consent or knowledge of the other joint tenants. Severance operates on the equitable interest, not the legal estate.

276. A buyer's solicitor is checking whether the seller's existing mortgage will be discharged on completion. She also wants to see whether any lease of part of the building has been granted out of the title. Which register records both a registered legal charge and a registered lease?

A. The charges register, which records the burdens affecting the registered estate

B. The property register, which records the extent and the benefits enjoyed

C. The proprietorship register, which records ownership and the class of title

D. The title plan, which records the land coloured or edged on the map

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (The charges register, which records the burdens affecting the registered estate): the charges register records burdens, including legal charges, restrictive covenants, easements burdening the land, notices protecting third party interests and registered leases. Option C is wrong because the proprietorship register deals with the class of title, the proprietor's name and any restrictions, so a restriction arising from a charge might appear there but the charge itself does not. The property register and the title plan describe the land and its benefits rather than encumbrances.

277. Six adult members of a family wish to buy a large house together and want all six names to appear at HM Land Registry as owners of the legal estate. Their solicitor explains that this cannot be done in the way they expect. Which statement correctly explains the position?

A. Only four may be registered, and the legal estate may be held as tenants in common

B. All six may be registered, provided a form A restriction is entered on the title

C. Only four may be registered, and the legal estate is always held as joint tenants

D. Only two may be registered, because capital money must be paid to two trustees

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (Only four may be registered, and the legal estate is always held as joint tenants): the legal estate is always held on a joint tenancy on trust, and there may be no more than four legal owners, so four of the six are registered as trustees holding for all six in equity. Option A is wrong because the legal estate can never be held as a tenancy in common; it is only the equitable interest that varies. The two trustee rule concerns giving a good receipt for capital money, not the maximum number of proprietors.

278. A solicitor is drafting the contract for the sale of a warehouse in Wakefield between two trading companies. She wants to incorporate the standard form conditions ordinarily used in a transaction of this kind, and then to amend them by special conditions the parties have negotiated. Which conditions should she incorporate?

A. The Standard Conditions of Sale, which apply to every sale of land

B. The Law Society protocol conditions, which govern all registered land sales

C. The Land Registry standard form conditions annexed to the transfer deed

D. The Standard Commercial Property Conditions, amended by the special conditions agreed

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (The Standard Commercial Property Conditions, amended by the special conditions agreed): the Standard Commercial Property Conditions are the standard form used commercially, and in a commercial deal the parties negotiate the contract rather than simply accepting the standard form, so special conditions amend them. Option A is wrong because the Standard Conditions of Sale are the residential form and are not the usual choice for a warehouse sale between companies. There are no Land Registry contract conditions and no separate protocol conditions of that kind.

279. Two parties negotiate the sale of a farm in Lincolnshire through a long exchange of emails in which every term is eventually agreed. Nothing is ever signed. They then meet and shake hands on the price. The seller now refuses to proceed. Does a binding contract for the sale of the land exist?

A. Yes, because all of the terms were agreed between them in writing

B. No, because it must be written, contain all terms and be signed

C. Yes, because part performance is demonstrated by the conduct of the parties

D. No, because a contract for the sale of land must be a deed

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (No, because it must be written, contain all terms and be signed): a contract for the sale of an interest in land must be in writing, incorporate all the terms the parties have agreed and be signed by or on behalf of each party, and an unsigned exchange of emails followed by a handshake does not satisfy that. Option A is wrong because writing alone is not enough without signature by or for both parties. A contract for sale need not be a deed; it is the transfer that must be.

280. A candidate is writing an attendance note after a property interview in which the client mentioned that an unnamed friend abroad would be wiring most of the purchase money. The candidate is deciding how to handle the point in the note. What should the note do?

A. Record the client's account of the funding without further comment or analysis

B. Name the concern, name the step to be taken, and name the limits on disclosure

C. Record that the friend must be added to the contract as a joint buyer

D. Record that the money will be accepted once it arrives in cleared funds

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (Name the concern, name the step to be taken, and name the limits on disclosure): where the facts raise money laundering the note should deal with it explicitly by naming the concern, naming the step, such as further evidence of source of funds or an internal report, and naming the limit on what may be said. Option A is wrong because silence where a red flag is plain loses marks on the ethics criterion and leaves the file exposed. Adding the friend to the contract does not address the funding concern at all.

281. A buyer's solicitor is reviewing the official copies of the title being bought. She sees a right of way in favour of the neighbouring farm across the rear of the garden, and separately a right of drainage enjoyed by the property over the neighbour's field. Where does each appear on the register?

A. Both appear in the property register, which lists rights benefiting the land

B. Both appear in the charges register, which lists the burdens on the land

C. The right of way in the charges register, the drainage in the property register

D. The right of way in the property register, the drainage in the charges register

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (The right of way in the charges register, the drainage in the property register): the property register records rights that benefit the land, while the charges register records burdens, including easements granted over the land in favour of somebody else. Option D is wrong because it reverses that division and would have the register recording the neighbour's right as a benefit to the buyer. Treating all easements as appearing in one register misses the point that benefit and burden are recorded separately.

282. A solicitor acting for a buyer notes a form A restriction on the seller's title. There are two registered proprietors, both alive, both of full capacity and both signing the transfer deed. The buyer asks whether the restriction creates a problem for the purchase. What is the correct advice?

A. It does, because the sale needs the consent of the equitable beneficiaries

B. It does not, because two trustees can give a valid receipt

C. It does, because a restriction must be cancelled before any sale completes

D. It does not, because a form A restriction concerns leases only

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (It does not, because two trustees can give a valid receipt): a form A restriction signals a tenancy in common in equity, and the requirement it imposes is satisfied where capital money is paid to two trustees, so two surviving proprietors signing the transfer causes no difficulty. Option A is wrong because the point of paying two trustees is that the equitable interests are overreached and lifted off the land, so the beneficiaries' consent is not needed. A form A restriction relates to co ownership of the beneficial interest and not to leases.

283. A solicitor is instructed by a couple buying a house. During the interview the woman says quietly that the deposit is entirely her money, that she does not want a joint tenancy, and that her partner has been pressing her hard to agree to one. The partner disagrees openly. What should the solicitor do?

A. Recognise a conflict, and decline to act for both without independent advice

B. Proceed on the basis of a joint tenancy, since that is the usual arrangement

C. Take instructions from the partner, who is conducting the negotiation with the agent

D. Complete a declaration of trust in her favour without informing the other client

Answer: A

The correct answer is A (Recognise a conflict, and decline to act for both without independent advice): where the interests of two co buyers actually conflict, or one appears to be under pressure, the solicitor cannot simply act for both, and independent advice is required. Option D is wrong because acting secretly for one client against the other's interests breaches the duty owed to each and compounds the conflict rather than resolving it. Choosing the usual arrangement or taking instructions from only one of two clients ignores the conflict entirely.

284. A buyer's solicitor finds two covenants in the charges register, given by an earlier owner. The first is not to use the property other than as a single private dwelling. The second is to contribute one half of the cost of maintaining a shared private driveway. Which statement is correct?

A. Neither covenant can bind the buyer, since both were given by a predecessor

B. Both covenants bind the buyer automatically as successor in title to the covenantor

C. The restrictive covenant may bind; the positive one is not directly enforceable

D. The positive covenant may bind; a restrictive covenant is personal to the covenantor

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (The restrictive covenant may bind; the positive one is not directly enforceable): the burden of a restrictive covenant can run with the land in equity and bind a successor, whereas the burden of a positive covenant does not run directly, which is why indirect devices such as an indemnity chain or a mutual benefit and burden arrangement are used. Option B is wrong because it treats both types alike and ignores the fundamental distinction. Restrictive covenants are not personal, and both entries must be read and reported on.

285. A seller has failed to complete and a notice to complete served by the buyer has now expired. The buyer has found an alternative property but has incurred wasted costs on searches and removals. She asks what remedies are available to her. Which answer best states the buyer's position?

A. She may forfeit the seller's deposit and recover her wasted expenditure incurred

B. She may only claim compensation at the contract rate for the seller's delay

C. She must complete the purchase and then sue the seller for damages afterwards

D. She may rescind, recover the deposit with interest and claim her damages

Answer: D

The correct answer is D (She may rescind, recover the deposit with interest and claim her damages): a buyer faced with a defaulting seller after an expired notice to complete may rescind, recover the deposit with interest and claim damages, or alternatively seek specific performance if she still wants the property. Option A is wrong because the deposit is paid by the buyer and there is no seller's deposit for her to forfeit. She is not obliged to complete before she can claim, and her remedies are not limited to contract rate compensation.

286. A developer holds an option to buy a field in Herefordshire, granted for value by the registered proprietor. The developer is not in occupation and does nothing on the land. Her solicitor wants to make certain that the option binds anyone who later buys the field. Which entry achieves that?

A. A restriction in the proprietorship register requiring the developer's written consent

B. A notice in the charges register protecting the priority of the option

C. An entry in the property register describing the developer's future right

D. A caution against first registration lodged at the local land charges registry

Answer: B

The correct answer is B (A notice in the charges register protecting the priority of the option): a notice is the entry that protects the priority of a third party interest such as an option or an equitable easement, so that a later disponee takes subject to it. Option A is wrong because a restriction controls whether a disposition can be registered at all, rather than preserving the priority of the interest itself. A caution against first registration is only relevant to unregistered land, and the property register records benefits, not third party burdens.

287. On an unregistered purchase the buyer's solicitor finds a legal easement of drainage granted by deed in 1974, and an equitable restrictive covenant created in 1988 which was never registered as a land charge against the covenantor's name. Which statement about the buyer's position is correct?

A. Both bind the buyer because each was created by a validly executed deed

B. Neither binds the buyer because neither was protected by any registration

C. The legal easement binds; the unregistered covenant is void against the buyer

D. The covenant binds; a legal easement requires registration to bind a buyer

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (The legal easement binds; the unregistered covenant is void against the buyer): in unregistered land legal easements and legal mortgages bind the world without registration, while a post 1925 restrictive covenant is a land charge and is void against a purchaser for value of a legal estate if not registered against the estate owner's name. Option A is wrong because execution by deed governs whether the right was validly created, not whether it survives against a later purchaser. Option D reverses the rule for legal easements, which need no entry to bind.

288. An unmarried couple are buying a house. He is contributing eighty per cent of the price from the sale of his flat and she is contributing the rest. He has two children from an earlier relationship whom he wants to benefit on his death. What should the solicitor advise about the equitable interest?

A. A joint tenancy, so that the survivor is fully protected on the first death

B. A joint tenancy, with a separate side letter recording the unequal contributions

C. A tenancy in common, with a declaration of trust recording their respective shares

D. A tenancy in common, with the legal estate vested in him alone as sole proprietor

Answer: C

The correct answer is C (A tenancy in common, with a declaration of trust recording their respective shares): unequal contributions and a wish to leave a share to someone other than the co owner both point to a tenancy in common with a declaration of trust recording the shares, so that the share passes under his will. Option A is wrong because survivorship would defeat his intention to benefit his children entirely. Option D is wrong because vesting the legal estate in him alone would leave her off the title with no second trustee to join in a sale and give a good receipt for capital money, so her interest would be exposed on any later dealing.

289. A solicitor is reading the lease of a first floor flat in a converted house. The tenant covenants to repair the interior. The landlord covenants to repair the roof and the main structure. Nothing anywhere in the lease mentions the wooden staircase serving the two flats. Why does that matter to the buyer?

A. The landlord is liable for the staircase because it lies outside the flat

B. The tenant is liable for the staircase because the tenant uses it daily

C. The point is immaterial, since the service charge covers all shared parts
